articles.title: Why Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid reportedly told Josh Simmons to leave a Chiefs meeting after heated exchange
articles.summary: Josh Simmons’ difficult start to life with the Kansas City Chiefs has taken another turn after a reported confrontation with head coach Andy Reid during a
articles.body: Josh Simmons’ difficult start to life with the Kansas City Chiefs has taken another turn after a reported confrontation with head coach Andy Reid during a team meeting. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes also told the offensive tackle to leave the room, according to a report from NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport, cited by Bleacher Report. The incident reportedly happened Wednesday, when Reid challenged Simmons over his posture during the meeting. Simmons explained that he was dealing with back and hip pain. He later apologised to Reid and his teammates, but the episode has added another layer to his frustrating season.Josh Simmons’ exchange with Andy Reid led to his exitAccording to the report, Simmons was sitting with his feet raised in the offensive meeting room when Reid asked him to put them down. Simmons responded that his back and hips were aching, which made sitting that way more comfortable.Reid then told the young tackle to seek treatment from the team’s athletic trainers if he was experiencing pain. The exchange escalated to the point that Mahomes also told Simmons he should leave the meeting, according to the report. Simmons exited the room and later apologised to both Reid and his teammates.The reported disagreement was not simply about a player’s seating position. It put Simmons in a difficult spot as he tries to establish himself in Kansas City while dealing with an injury that has kept him off the field. Reid’s response also reflected the expectations inside a team meeting, where players are expected to follow the coach’s instructions even when they have concerns of their own.There is no reported indication that the incident alone led to Simmons’ subsequent roster move. The available account describes the exchange and his apology, but does not establish any further disciplinary action.Simmons’ injury setback leaves the Chiefs with another problemKansas City placed Simmons on injured reserve on Thursday, according to Bleacher Report. The 2025 first-round pick had already seen his rookie season cut short by a fractured wrist. A bulging disk in his back has prevented him from playing in 2026, leaving the team waiting for him to make meaningful progress in his recovery.Chiefs trainer Rick Burkholder offered a more detailed picture of that process this week. He said Simmons had been working hard and had improved enough to return to limited practice last week, but his rehabilitation had since stalled.“He worked diligently with my staff every day and has improved to point where he could return to practice in a limited capacity last week,” Burkholder said. “However, we feel like he's plateaued in the rehab process as he's trying to get to the final steps of recovery with the return to competition. He's just not there yet.”That is the more pressing issue for Kansas City. Simmons was drafted in the first round to address a key need on the offensive line, but the Chiefs have instead turned to undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson at left tackle. Simmons’ injured reserve placement means he will miss at least four more weeks, according to the report.For Simmons, the immediate challenge is to get healthy and return to the field. The reported meeting incident has drawn attention, but his recovery remains the central concern for a Chiefs team that still needs the young tackle to deliver on his potential.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jonathan Taylor's Wife Ayanna Teases Mystery Around Colts Trade Rumors in Viral Video, RB Responds
articles.summary: Amid the trade rumors surrounding Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor, his wife added more fuel to the fire.
articles.body:
Amid the trade rumors surrounding Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor, his wife added more fuel to the fire.

Ayanna Taylor posted a now-viral video on social media revealing that "players that once seemed untouchable," like her husband, "may now be on the table" in potential trades. She went on to tease, "There's more to the story."

In her "Part 2" video , Ayanna Taylor went on to reference the Colts firing general manager Chris Ballard following their 2-4 start and their lost 2027 first-round draft pick after their trade with the New York Jets, which acquired cornerback Sauce Gardner.

"So let's look at the situation that they've put themselves in: they have a losing record, they just fired their 10-year GM and they have no draft picks. ... So let's think about it, what do you do when you don't have what you need and you don't have money to pay for it? ... You trade. That's what brings us back to my husband," she said.

Taylor was asked about the video after Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings, saying he needs to "stay focused."

ESPN's Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter reported on Sunday that the Green Bay Packers, Seattle Seahawks, Vikings, and Denver Broncos are expected to "ponder the possibility" of acquiring Taylor before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. The Athletic's Jonathan Jones also reported that "sources believe the New York Giants and Vikings could be potential suitors" for the three-time Pro Bowler.

Any further struggles by the Colts could lead the team to blow up their roster and commit to a rebuild. Taylor would undoubtedly be the biggest trade piece Indianapolis has to offer, so his days with the franchise could be numbered, as his wife predicted.

articles.title: La NFL se estrena en París con Aaron Rodgers en plan estrella a sus 42 años
articles.standfirst: Los Pittsburgh Steelers derrotan por 16-10 a los New Orleans Saints en el Stade de France
articles.summary: Los Pittsburgh Steelers derrotan por 16-10 a los New Orleans Saints en el Stade de France
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers guió este domingo a los Pittsburgh Steelers al triunfo por 16-10 sobre los New Orleans Saints en el primer partido de temporada de la NFL en la historia disputado en París. En el encuentro, que se disputó sin contratiempos en el Stade de France, Rodgers, cuatro veces MVP de la temporada, pasó para 212 yardas y un envío de anotación. Con la victoria, tercera consecutiva, los Steelers se colocaron con cinco triunfos y dos derrotas en la cima de la división Norte de la Conferencia Americana, mientras que los Saints quedaron con marca de 2-5 en el tercer puesto del Sur de la Conferencia Nacional. La ofensiva de los Steelers tuvo un inicio dominante sobre la defensiva de los Saints, a la que arrastraron 51 yardas en ocho jugadas con Jaylen Warren como el ariete que se apuntó 43 de esas yardas, pero se atascaron dentro de la zona roja y se conformaron con un gol de campo de 28 yardas que convirtió Chris Boswell para tomar ventaja de 3-0. En el segundo cuarto, Tyler Shough movió al ataque de los Saints en una serie que recorrió 62 yardas para que Daniel Carlson empatara el partido 3-3 luego de conectar una patada de tres puntos de 38 yardas. El equipo de Pittsburh recuperó la ventaja (10-3) con un pase de Aaron Rodgers a las diagonales que atrapó Darnell Washington, en una serie en la que fue clave una conexión de Rodgers con DK Metcalf de 51 yardas que dejó a su equipo dentro de la yarda cinco del territorio de los Saints. Con este pase de anotación, Rodgers se convirtió en el tercer pasador con más envíos de 'touchdown' en la historia de la NFL, con 540, aún lejos de Drew Brees, segundo con más envíos a las diagonales, con 571, y Tom Brady, el primero, con 649. El equipo de Nueva Orleans volvió a establecer su ofensiva, que atravesó 51 yardas hasta la anotación de Devaughn Vele, quien atrapó un envío de Shough que igualó el juego 10-10. Los Steelers se fueron al descanso con ventaja de 13-10 luego de que Chris Boswell convirtiera un gol de campo de 47 yardas en el último segundo del periodo. En el inicio del tercer cuarto los Saints se comieron la mitad del reloj en una ofensiva que amenazaba con terminar en anotación, pero a 10 yardas de las diagonales Shough fue interceptado por Payton Wilson, acierto que el ataque de los Steelers convirtió en tres puntos más, 16-10, con un gol de campo de Boswell que significó la victoria. Antes del inicio de este partido, Roger Goodell, comisionado de la NFL, dijo que no tenía dudas de que la liga regresará a París con otro partido de temporada regular. Goodell lo afirmó a pesar de que la NFL canceló varias actividades con aficionados el sábado anterior debido a las protestas que la capital francesa ha sufrido de manera recurrente desde hace un par de semanas.

articles.title: NFL Paris 2026: Aaron Rodgers leads Pittsburgh Steelers past New Orleans Saints in first-ever game in France
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers beat the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in the first-ever NFL regular-season game to be played in Paris; Aaron Rodgers passes Peyton Manning for the third-most touchdown passes in NFL history
articles.body:
The four-time MVP quarterback surpassed Manning's tally of 539 touchdown passes with a first-half strike to tight end Darnell Washington and finished the game 19 of 30 for 212 yards as Mike McCarthy's Steelers improved to 5-2 on the year.

Saints quarterback Tyler Shough went 30 of 38 for 278 yards, a touchdown pass to Devaughn Vele and a second-half interception as Kellen Moore's side, honouring their deep-rooted French ties this week, dropped to 2-5.

Pittsburgh's Terrible Towels flew proudly while travelling Saints translated NOLA noise to Europe as the Stade de France welcomed 78,488 fans for the sixth of nine international games this season, Paris one of three first-time hosts for 2026 alongside Melbourne and Rio de Janeiro.

Civil unrest in France had dominated build-up to Sunday's game after what began as peaceful demonstrations had turned into violence and looting, resulting in the cancellation of fan events and prompting an increased security presence across the city.

Still, an undeterred crowd would serenade more NFL history with another electric atmosphere reflect of the league's reach overseas, albeit bolstered by a significant travelling party from both Pittsburgh and New Orleans.

Chris Boswell was a perfect three of three on field goals, while Saints counterpart Daniel Carlson was guilty of a costly miss.

Trailing 13-10 at the break, the Saints saw their immediate reply come up empty when Shough was intercepted by Payton Wilson to end a 14-play drive that had knocked a costly seven-and-a-half minutes off the clock.

Rodgers would later joke in his press conference about how Wilson intercepted him on a near-identical play during practice earlier in the week.

"I nearly took that one to the house," laughed Wilson.

Chase Young kept his team alive on the ensuing possession when the Saints sack leader swarmed Rodgers to stall the drive on third-and-10, Boswell coming out to kick a 39-yard field goal.

The Saints, though, were denied a chance to cut into Pittsburgh's lead again when Daniel Carlson missed a 52-yard field goal with 10 minutes remaining. Carlson had notably arrived in Paris on his own late this week, with his wife due to give birth back home.

Boswell had delivered the first-ever points scored in Paris with a 28-yard field goal at the end of Pittsburgh's opening drive, before giving his team a 13-10 lead with his 47-yard effort as time expired in the second quarter.

Carlson drew the Saints level at 3-3 with a 38-yard field goal after Shough had flipped the field with a 49-yard strike to Barion Brown.

Pittsburgh tight end Washington scored the first-ever touchdown in Paris when he treated the French crowd to a tinge of Randy Moss while out-muscling a helpless Kool-Aid McKinstry for a four-yard grab at the side of the end zone. His exhibition in bully ball would see Rodgers join Manning for the third-most touchdown passes in NFL history.

Rodgers himself had teed up the touchdown beautifully with a 51-yard strike to DK Metcalf after climbing the pocket and launching deep on the move to convert on third-and-14.

Shough capped his side's response with a one-yard touchdown pass to Vele inside the two-minute warning after the Saints had been stuffed at the one-yard line for three straight plays.

Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy: "I think the most important thing is you have a chance to travel as a team and the challenge of being on the road is always exciting, but this is special. I think everything that goes into this game, first time playing in France, and so it definitely brings a special feel to it. I think it's really good for your team; you have a chance to get on the road. It's been a joy to play here.

"I wouldn't say it (unrest in Paris) overshadowed the game, I know a lot of our team had families in France. I know everybody enjoyed Friday. With the uncertainty Saturday we stayed close to the hotel. France is a beautiful place. It's my first time here and I'd love the opportunity some day to come back and enjoy it."

Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers: "I've enjoyed the last two international games (Ireland and France), and then obviously London. For a long time in Green Bay we never got to go overseas because Lambeau is such an incredible home and they were never going to give up a home game and then we did in 2022. I've enjoyed it; I wish we could have enjoyed it both in Ireland and France for a little more time. It's great the game is growing."

Terron Armstead, former New Orleans Saints offensive tackle, on Sky Sports: "You definitely saw the difference between the two quarterbacks. Aaron Rodgers pretty much controlled the game. He was very solid, did nothing crazy and ultimately just took care of the ball. What it came down to was the Saints' inability to take care of the ball and score points when they got in the red zone. Turnovers will kill you every time."

articles.title: Malik Willis, Dolphins fend off Jets late to pick up first win of the season
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are now the only team in the NFL still without a win this fall.
articles.body:
At long last, Malik Willis and the Miami Dolphins won.

Willis and the Dolphins fended off a late push to beat the New York Jets 28-25 at MetLife Stadium on Sunday afternoon. The victory ends Miami's five-game losing skid to start the season. The win also brought the Dolphins out from the bottom of the league.

The Los Angeles Chargers are the only team in the league without a win.

Though it wasn't great, or even a complete game offensively, Willis and the Dolphins showed stretches of solid football — especially in the first half. They scored a touchdown on each of their first two drives of the afternoon, first on a 7-yard pass to Caleb Douglas and then on a 1-yard punch-in from Ollie Gordon. The opening touchdown was the first of Douglas' career.

The Dolphins pushed their lead to 14 points at the break. Willis scrambled into the end zone from 2 yards out in the final seconds of the second quarter to cap a 91-yard drive. It was easily Willis' best outing this season.

For some reason, that didn't carry over into the second half. Willis and the Dolphins stalled offensively for most of the third and fourth quarters. That left the door open for the Jets, who cut the deficit to a single score after an Omar Cooper Jr. touchdown grab in the third quarter. That was set up by a 60-yard reception he made earlier in the drive.

They should have tied the game in the fourth quarter, and got all the way to the goal line before the Dolphins came up with a huge stand. They stuffed the run twice and then sacked Geno Smith for a 12-yard loss on third down to force the field goal.

Finally, after completing only three passes in the second half, Willis found Douglas one last time. Willis dumped it off short to him on the left side, right before taking a huge hit in the backfield, and Douglass took off. He made it 63 yards up the sideline and into the end zone.

That still wasn't enough to seal the deal. The Jets got back within a field goal quickly, thanks to a Mason Taylor 12-yard touchdown catch and successful 2-point conversion. But the Dolphins quickly ended the game and converted a fourth-down run at midfield to kill the rest of the clock and escape with the three-point win.

Willis ended up going 14-of-21 passing for 208 yards with two touchdowns; all but four of those passes were completed in the first half. Gordon had 103 rushing yards and a score on 25 carries, and Greg Dulcich had 86 yards on five catches.

The victory was the first of head coach Jeff Hafley's career. The Dolphins hired Hafley to replace Mike McDaniel in January, marking Hafley's first head-coaching job in the league after his previous stint as the Green Bay Packers' defensive coordinator.

Smith went 23-of-30 passing for 287 yards with three touchdowns and an interception in the loss for the Jets (2-5). Braelon Allen had 104 yards on 17 carries, and Cooper had 115 yards and a score on his five catches. The Jets have lost five of their past six games, and will need a big turnaround if they are going to make any sort of playoff push in the back half of the season.

Similarly, the Dolphins still have a long way to go to salvage this season. It won't get any easier, either, with Drake Maye and the New England Patriots up next in Week 8. But finally winning a game, and beating a division rival in the process, is a great first step.

articles.title: Falcons LB Kendal Daniels, a week after scary neck injury, recovers fumble late to help lift Atlanta past San Francisco
articles.summary: Kendal Daniels was carted off the field last week after a scary neck injury he suffered against the Chicago Bears.
articles.body:
Kendal Daniels appears to be perfectly fine.

Daniels, just a week removed from a scary neck injury that forced him to be stretchered off the field , came up with a game-sealing fumble recovery on Sunday afternoon to lift the Atlanta Falcons past the San Francisco 49ers .

The Falcons were up by nine late at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, trying to fend off one last-ditch effort from the 49ers. With less than a minute left, San Francisco tight end George Kittle caught a wide open pass and was breaking to the middle of the field, seemingly putting the 49ers into scoring position.

But Jessie Bates dove for Kittle's legs and managed to just barely trip him up. As he was stumbling forward, Kittle lost the ball — which allowed Daniels to fly in and land on it untouched.

That secured the 29-20 win for the Falcons, and officially handed the 49ers their first loss of the season.

Daniels ended up leading the Falcons with a career-high 11 total tackles on Sunday, nine of which he did by himself. While the fumble recovery was the most important, he was a force for the Atlanta defense all afternoon. He even intercepted 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy late in the fourth quarter, which was one of four turnovers they forced all day.

Daniels, who the Falcons took in the fourth round of the NFL Draft out of Oklahoma, is now up to 40 total tackles this season.

But Sunday's outing came on the heels of what was a scary looking injury in their Week 7 matchup with the Chicago Bears. Daniels came flying in to try and tackle Bears tight end Colston Loveland, and he remained down on the field for roughly 10 minutes before being carted off.

But just days later, Daniels was back at practice and had been cleared to return.

"I scared a lot of people," Daniels said, via the Atlanta Journal-Constitution . "It was a scary play. I'm blessed to come out how I did, and it was a bang-bang play, but I'm happy I'm here."

The Falcons now sit at 3-4 on the season after Sunday's win. They'll take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers next week in Florida.

And Daniels, now with his terrifying neck injury clearly behind him, can keep pushing forward in what has been an already impressive rookie campaign.

articles.title: Miami Dolphins no longer winless after defeating New York Jets
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins are no longer among the winless teams in the NFL. The Dolphins never trailed in a 28-25 victory over the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins are no longer among the winless teams in the NFL.

After never leading at any point in any game this season, the Dolphins (1-5) never trailed in a 28-25 victory Sunday over the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium.

Miami turned a 7-7 game into a 21-7 halftime lead before Chop Robinson capped the team's best defensive stand of the season in the fourth quarter and preserved the lead.

Miami then hung on to give Jeff Hafley the first victory of his NFL head coaching career.

Miami Dolphins hope for first NFL win at New York Jets

Miami's win means the Los Angeles Chargers (0-6) remain the lone winless team in the league. The Chargers were off Sunday.

How bad was it for the Jets (2-5)? A fan was shown with a paper bag over his head that read: "Not even Miami?"

Miami returns home Sunday, Nov. 1, to face New England (4-3). The Patriots are coming off a Thursday night loss at Chicago.

Here are five instant takeaways from the Dolphins' first win of the season:

Rookie receiver Caleb Douglas returns from injury with a big game

Caleb Douglas, a third-round draft pick from Texas Tech, played for the first time after suffering an ankle injury in Week 2 and recorded the first two touchdowns of his career, scoring on his only two catches.

Douglas, who started his college career at Florida, scored on the opening drive on a 7-yard pass from Malik Willis. Douglas then scored what became the game-winning touchdown with 4:44 remaining on a 63-yard catch-and-run in which he tip-toed the sideline around midfield as former Dolphins safety Minkah Fitzpatrick attempted to shove him out of bounds.

It took six games but Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley got his first win as an NFL head coach. And it could not have come in a better spot.

The game in the Meadowlands was 17 miles from Hafley's hometown of Montvale, N.J. His mom, brother and sister were in the stadium, as were about 30 other friends and family members. They all witnessed the biggest victory of Hafley's career.

The Dolphins looked like anything but one of two remaining winless teams in the NFL entering Week 7. They dominated early, leading 21-7 at the half and outgaining the Jets, 231-114, in the first 30 minutes with a very balanced offense. Miami then held on for the win.

"The offense did a great job in every one of their possessions," Hafley told CBS at halftime. "Malik is using his legs, he's throwing the ball well. We settled down on defense after we busted that first drive (allowing the Jets to drive down the field and tie the game at 7). We just got to come out and be consistent and keep doing what we're doing."

Hafley three-times went for a first down on fourth down and was 3-for-3. The biggest came at the end of the game after the two-minute warning when Willis got 2-yards with the ball on the Jets 49.

In the first half, Ollie Gordon's 1-yard touchdown on fourth down gave Miami a 14-7 lead, and Willis scrambled for 5 yards on 4th-and-2 from the Jets' 41, extending Miami's third TD drive.

Hafley was hired by GM Jon-Eric Sullivan, 10 days after Sullivan came to Miami. They knew each other well having worked together in Green Bay, Sullivan as the VP Player Personnel and Hafley the defensive coordinator. While they embarked on a very deliberate rebuild, no one knew how the season would unfold.

As CBS went to a commercial after Miami drove 76 yards on the game's opening drive for a touchdown, Foreigner's "Feels Like the First Time" was playing. The reason: It marked the first time Miami held a lead this season. The Dolphins were the only team entering Week 7 that had not led at any point in a game.

That lead, which came on a 7-yard pass from Willis to Douglas, lasted all of 2:16 as the Jets needed just four plays to drive 65 yards to tie the score. Miami regained the touchdown lead again on a 1-yard Gordon run with less than a minute to play in the first quarter. This time the lead held for good.

Malik Willis in control with zero turnovers

Willis had his best half with the Dolphins in the first 30 minutes and held steady in the second half. The five-year veteran entered the game with a 68.4 passer rating and had a first-half rating of 132.9 after completing 10-of-13 passes for 128 yards. He closed 14 of 21 for 208 yards, 2 touchdown passes and a 130.7 rating.

More importantly, Willis protected the ball. He entered with four interceptions and five fumbles. The Dolphins did not commit a turnover against the Jets. Early on, Willis received great protection, often times throwing from a clean pocket. Willis was sacked twice in the second half.

Chop Robinson, defense tightens late in the game

The Jets were 1-yard from completely erasing the Dolphins' two-touchdown lead before Miami's most impressive defensive stand of the season.

The Jets went from first-and-goal at the 1 to fourth down from the 15 after Chop Robinson chased down Jets quarterback Geno Smith for a 12-yard sack, forcing New York to settle for a field goal to make the score 21-17.

Miami got key tackles from Zach Sieler on first down and Josh Uche on second down, both for losses of 1-yard before Robinson's sack.

The Jets went 3-and-out on their next series and cut the Dolphins lead to three with a late touchdown and two-point conversion, but Miami was able to run out the clock.

articles.title: Where Titans land after loss vs Browns for NFL draft order
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans are in the race to get the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft after Week 7.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans went back to their losing ways Oct. 25 with a last-second, 27-24 home defeat against the Cleveland Browns, moving them up to second in the standings for the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.

A week after their first win of the season, 26-20 against the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 18, the Titans fell to 1-6 and moved from third to second in terms of where they currently are in the NFL draft order, per tankathon . The Titans last held the No. 1 pick in 2025.

According to tankathon.com , the Los Angeles Chargers (0-6), who did not play this week, would have the top pick based on their strength of schedule, which is the weakest among the worst teams in the NFL. The Miami Dolphins (1-5) picked up their first win of the season Oct. 25 against the Jets, but their strength of schedule is better than the Titans'.

articles.title: Browns win on walk-off field goal for second straight week, defeating Titans 27-24
articles.summary: For the second consecutive week, Deshaun Watson led a game-winning drive finished off by a field goal as time expired from Andre Szmyt.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns won their second consecutive game on a final drive and walk-off field goal. Andre Szmyt kicked a 32-yarder as time expired for a 27-24 win over the Tennessee Titans.

Cleveland's Week 7 victory follows a 13-10 win against the Baltimore Ravens, which also ended on a Szmyt field goal with no time remaining. That kick was from 37 yards, completing a comeback from a 10-point deficit .

Deshaun Watson threw for 308 yards, completing 25 of 36 passes with 1 interception. He completed all three of his passes on the Browns' final drive, including a 36-yard catch-and-run by tight end Harold Fannin.

KC Concepcion notched 8 receptions for 129 yards, while Quinshon Judkins rushed for 96 yards on 17 carries.

With the win, the Browns improve to 5-2 and are tied for first place in the AFC North with the Pittsburgh Steelers, who defeated the New Orleans Saints 16-10 earlier on Sunday in Paris.

Titans nearly took early two-touchdown lead

Tennessee scored touchdowns on their first two possessions, helped by an interception by Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson. The Titans opened by moving 65 yards in six plays, finished off with a 15-yard pass from Cam Ward to Carnell Tate followed by a 36-yard touchdown run by Tony Pollard.

Following an interception by Cor'Dale Flott on Cleveland's first drive, Pollard scored his second TD four plays later with a 10-yard rush.

Tennessee nearly had a two-touchdown lead after its defense forced a three-and-out toward the end of the first quarter. After advancing 53 yards on 11 plays, Pollard appeared to have his third TD on a 3-yard rush up the middle. However, the play was reviewed and Pollard's knee was ruled to be down before the ball crossed the goal line.

With three plays from the 1-yard line, the Titans could not punch the ball in for a score. Ward was stopped on a push up the middle, then was sacked on the next play. With a fourth-and-goal, Titans coach Robert Saleh opted to go for the TD but Pollard was stopped on an inside run by linebacker Winston Reid.

Both teams exchanged turnovers on their next respective possessions with Fannin fumbling for Cleveland and Denzel Ward getting an interception for the Browns on the next play.

Cleveland then tied the score at 14-14 with a 78-yard drive highlighted by 21-yard and 32-yard completions from Watson to Concepcion. Judkins finished off the series with a 6-yard TD run. The Browns took the lead on their next possession on a 28-yard field goal by Szymt.

The Titans got a game-tying field goal on a 29-yarder from Joey Slye with 8:41 remaining in the fourth quarter. But Cleveland took the lead on its next possession, finishing off a 71-yard series with Watson running 9 yards for the score.

Tennessee responded with a touchdown drive of its own with Cam Ward completing passes of 14 yards, 26 yards and 18 yards before Pollard got his third TD of the game on a 1-yard run.

New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo's longest run of his career came with a price.

Skattebo told ESPN's Dan Graziano that he suffered a hamstring injury during his 42-yard run that helped set up Devin Singletary's game-winning 30-yard touchdown in Sunday's 27-21 overtime win over the Houston Texans.

"Good thing we have a bye week," Skattebo told Graziano.

Despite the good vibes from Sunday's win, Skattebo's admission dampens things a bit. The 24-year-old was limited to eight games during his rookie season after suffering a dislocated ankle, so it would be disappointing to see him miss time with another injury during his sophomore campaign.

Skattebo led the Giants with 17 carries for a career-high 124 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's win. It was his first career 100-yard game, and it helped the Giants improve to 4-2-1, maintaining their lead in the NFC East in what was expected to be a rebuilding year.

In addition to Skattebo's big performance and Singletary's game-winning score, the Giants also got rushing touchdowns from Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Jameis Winston, the latter of whom had four carries after losing his starting quarterback job to J.J. McCarthy. In all, New York totaled 188 yards on the ground.

The Giants will be on a bye in Week 8 before returning to action against the Philadelphia Eagles on Nov. 8, so Skattebo will have some extra time to recover from his hamstring injury before getting back on the field.

"No, I have not thought about a quarterback change," Colts head coach Shane Steichen said after Sunday's loss to the Minnesota Vikings. "Because I got a ton of faith in Daniel. The game plan today was to go in and run the football, and obviously at the end he had the interception, and that happens in football."

Jones had his worst game of the season on Sunday, throwing for just 108 yards on 13-of-22 passing with no touchdowns. He had a costly interception on the Colts' final offensive drive of the game as they trailed 16-10.

If Steichen decides to bench Jones, the next option would be Anthony Richardson, who appeared in just two games last year. Richardson, who played in 11 games in 2024, had 1,814 yards, eight touchdowns and 12 interceptions the last time he was the starter.

Jones has been significantly worse than he was during his breakout season in 2025, but it appears Steichen is giving him a long leash to turn things around.

articles.title: Everything J.J. McCarthy Said About Winning 1st Start as Giants QB Since Vikings Trade
articles.summary: With J.J. McCarthy making his first start after being traded from the Minnesota Vikings, the New York Giants downed the Houston Texans 27-21 in overtime on Sunday.
articles.body:
With J.J. McCarthy making his first start after being traded from the Minnesota Vikings, the New York Giants downed the Houston Texans 27-21 in overtime on Sunday.

McCarthy didn't light up the box score, but he was more than happy with the result of the game.

"Truly the only stat I care about is going 1-0," McCarthy said after the win. "I could care less how we get it done. At the end of the day, you want to perform well, you want to execute well and it's one of those things where, if the running backs are getting their touchdowns, I'm as happy as I can be. Whether I'm throwing the touchdowns, I'm as happy as I can be."

McCarthy added that "it's a lot of fun" getting to play for the Giants.

"So much fun to be out there playing football, but with this group, it makes it that much more fun," he said.

McCarthy also gave a speech to his team after getting a game ball, saying "this is just the f--king beginning" while saying the roster is "so talented":

McCarthy threw for 252 yards on 20-of-28 passing in his first start for the Vikings. That followed a 243-yard, touchdown-scoring performance in the fourth quarter alone against the New Orleans Saints last week.

"I thought he did a great job. He's not a guy that's never played before. He's young, but he's played," head coach John Harbaugh said. "And he showed it. He made throws. I'm sure he didn't play perfect, but he played a heck of a football game; he deserves a lot of credit."

It was the ground game that got the job done for New York in the overtime win, though. Cam Skattebo rushed for 124 yards and a touchdown on 17 carries, while Devin Singletary and Tyrone Tracy Jr. each added a score as well. Backup quarterback Jameis Winston also came in and rushed for a touchdown.

In overtime, Singletary scored the game-winning touchdown on a 30-yard rush.

"I definitely had the best view in the building," McCarthy said. "Being able to see him hit those gaps and make those cuts, they just didn't stop. They looked like it was the first play of the game when they were hitting those holes. It's just a blessing to be a part of a group like that and have a running back group like that."

McCarthy has had a rough start to his career, missing all of his rookie season before struggling in Minnesota last year, but he appears ready to turn the corner in New York.

It's fair to say that he's earned the starting job for another week, and he'll look to continue getting comfortable during the bye week before returning to action against the Philadelphia Eagles.

articles.title: Travis Kelce eyes NFL history with 15,379 career receiving yards as 2 major milestones loom against the Seahawks
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has another chance to make NFL history, and the Kansas City Chiefs’ Sunday night clash with the Seattle Seahawks could become a defining
articles.body: Travis Kelce has another chance to make NFL history, and the Kansas City Chiefs’ Sunday night clash with the Seattle Seahawks could become a defining moment in his remarkable career. The veteran tight end is on the verge of overtaking Tony Gonzalez’s record for career receiving yards by a tight end, including playoff games. With just 35 yards separating Kelce from the milestone, every catch could carry added significance. The Chiefs star also has an opportunity to climb further up the NFL’s all-time receptions list, strengthening his legacy among the league’s greatest pass catchers.Travis Kelce needs just 35 yards to surpass Tony GonzalezKelce enters the Seahawks matchup with 15,379 career receiving yards across the regular season and playoffs. Gonzalez finished his career with 15,413, leaving the Chiefs tight end just 35 yards short of the long-standing mark.The numbers highlight Kelce’s remarkable consistency. He has recorded 13,301 receiving yards during the regular season and another 2,078 in the playoffs. His postseason production has played a major role in pushing him close to Gonzalez’s overall total.Gonzalez, who built his Hall of Fame career with the Chiefs and Atlanta Falcons, set a standard that stood out even among the NFL’s most productive tight ends. Kelce now has a realistic opportunity to move past that benchmark while continuing to play a central role in Kansas City’s offence.The timing also adds intrigue. A strong performance under the Sunday Night Football spotlight would allow Kelce to reach the milestone in front of a national audience. He does not need an unusually productive night to get there. A few well-timed catches and a significant gain could be enough to put his name above Gonzalez’s in the record books.Travis Kelce eyes another NFL milestone in career receptionsThe receiving-yardage record is not the only achievement within Kelce’s reach against Seattle. He also has a chance to break into the top five on the NFL’s all-time regular-season receptions list.Kelce currently has 1,100 career regular-season catches. Cris Carter sits just ahead of him with 1,101, while Marvin Harrison has 1,102. Three receptions would take Kelce past both former stars and move him into fifth place in league history.The four players above that mark include Jerry Rice, who leads the list with 1,549 catches, followed by Larry Fitzgerald with 1,432, Gonzalez with 1,325 and Jason Witten with 1,228.Reaching the top five would underline another part of Kelce’s success. His value has never rested solely on spectacular plays or postseason performances. Year after year, he has remained a dependable target, giving his quarterbacks a reliable option in crucial situations.For Kansas City, Kelce’s pursuit of these records comes alongside the team’s immediate goal of securing a victory. articles.title: “Smart dude that has done a lot of great things": How Travis Kelce and godfather LaTroy Hawkins helped Patrick Mahomes build his business empire and secure his financial future beyond NFL
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes has built a successful career with the Kansas City Chiefs, but his plans go well beyond football.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has built a successful career with the Kansas City Chiefs, but his plans go well beyond football. The quarterback has invested in several businesses and sports teams while learning how to manage his money for the future. Two people have played different roles in shaping that approach: his godfather, former MLB pitcher LaTroy Hawkins, and his teammate and close friend Travis Kelce. While Hawkins taught Mahomes about financial responsibility, Kelce showed him the value of staying open to new opportunities.In a May 2024 interview with Boardroom, Mahomes discussed the lessons he has picked up while building his business portfolio. His comments offered a look at how advice from people close to him has influenced his decisions away from the field. LaTroy Hawkins taught Patrick Mahomes to think about life beyond his NFL salaryMahomes learned about professional sports long before he entered the NFL. His father, Pat Mahomes, played professional baseball, and his godfather LaTroy Hawkins spent 21 seasons in Major League Baseball. Hawkins also worked in the Minnesota Twins' front office after his playing career.Having people around him who understood professional sports helped Mahomes learn that a successful career requires more than talent. Hawkins guided him on professionalism and managing money, encouraging him to think about his financial future instead of focusing only on what he earned during his playing years.Mahomes also learned about saving money from his time around locker rooms. Despite becoming the 10th overall pick in the 2017 NFL Draft, he did not buy a car until his second contract. A local marketing deal provided him with a vehicle after the Chiefs selected him.That decision reflected the financial habits he had started developing early in his career. Rather than spending quickly after entering the league, Mahomes wanted to understand how to manage his earnings.In the Boardroom interview, he explained how education and experience shaped his investment decisions.“I think it all comes with education. I’ve learned from things I’ve done in the past, finding the positives and negatives and learning from people that I have around me, and then trying to be better in the next investment or product I endorse.”Mahomes has since built a portfolio that includes stakes in the Kansas City Royals, Kansas City Current and Sporting Kansas City, alongside his wife, Brittany. His investments also extend to companies and brands outside traditional team ownership.The quarterback has made it clear that he wants to understand the opportunities he takes rather than simply attach his name to a business. His experience with Hawkins helped him recognise the value of learning before making financial decisions. Travis Kelce showed Patrick Mahomes the value of business opportunities beyond footballTravis Kelce has also influenced how Mahomes approaches business. The two Kansas City Chiefs stars have developed a close friendship while building careers that extend beyond the NFL.Mahomes has watched Kelce expand his profile through commercial appearances, investments and other ventures. Their connection also reaches the business world, with both players investing in Alpine's Formula 1 team.Speaking about Kelce's development outside football, Mahomes said he was impressed by how his teammate had expanded his role.“He’s someone who’s expanded his role from off the football field to the status that he has now, including investments.”Mahomes also praised Kelce for carefully considering opportunities before making decisions. He said:“He does a great job of listening to every opportunity and then making the right decisions for himself.”The Chiefs quarterback also pushed back against the idea that Kelce's public image tells the whole story about him. While Kelce is known for his outgoing personality, Mahomes sees a thoughtful businessman behind it.“I always joke around that he puts on this persona that he’s this guy that just likes to party, go out, and have fun. But when he comes down to it, man, he’s a very smart dude that has done a lot of great things with his career on and off the field. That’s why he’s in the place that he’s at now.”Those observations reflect the lesson Mahomes has taken from watching his teammate. Staying open to opportunities can help athletes build careers and income streams that continue after they stop playing.Mahomes has applied that thinking to his own investments. In May 2024, he became the lead investor in Throne Sport Coffee, working with former BodyArmor executive Michael Fedele. articles.title: NFL's French national anthem performer Nina Tonji alters words to La Marseillaise, sparking outrage in France
articles.summary: Nina Tonji changed "impure" to "united" in La Marseillaise before the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints game amid immigration unrest.
articles.body: Words often matter as much as actions and amid the civil unrest that France has felt in recent days, some French people are apparently angry and offended over the altering of their national anthem before the NFL game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints. And, yes, this has to do with immigrants in France. Before the game, singer Nina Tonji performed La Marseillaise at the Stade de France. Although she received a warm round of applause afterward, there has been significant online backlash because she modified the lyrics of the song. NFL OVERCOMES CIVIL UNREST, TRUMP CONCERNS AND CALLS TO POSTPONE AS STEELERS AND SAINTS KICK OFF IN PARIS Tonji changed "Qu'un sang impur abreuve nos sillons!" to "Qu'un sang uni abreuve nos sillons!," and that was clearly done on purpose because it has political and societal ramifications. "Qu’un sang impur abreuve nos sillons" means "May impure blood water our furrows/fields." In the revolutionary context of La Marseillaise, "impure blood" referred to enemies and traitors – particularly French immigrants fighting alongside foreign armies. Replacing impur ("impure") with uni ("united") changes the meaning of the passage from from a call for enemy blood to nourish France’s soil into an appeal for national unity and solidarity that includes immigrants to nourish France's soil. Tonji thus changed the song's tone from violent exclusion of a foreign enemy to a message of unity with foreigners. She gave immigrants cover that La Marseillaise did not in 1792 when it was written during the French Revolution. And, yes, this rendition represented a lyrical alteration by the Tonji that departed from the traditional wording of the French national anthem. But it comes at a time when people in France are on edge about immigration and foreigners. That’s because at least some of the protesters who took to the streets during the past two weeks of civil unrest were immigrants. Some rallied for anti-Israel causes, while others called for the overthrow of the current political system. So, predictably, there has been an online backlash. This is where we also inform you that Tonji was born in Montreal, Canada. Much of the attention she is now getting has come from media accounts with massive followings. Cerfia posted the song to its 1.3 million followers and highlighted the changes made. RMC Sport posted it to its 2.7 million followers, saying the change caused "confusion." Francetvsport also posted the song to its 297,500 followers. The replies to the viral posts did include some people willing to overlook the change. But a vast majority insulted everything from Tonji's voice, to looks, to the action itself, calling it a "scandal," and "disrespectful" and a "controversy." Seems some French people have pride in their national anthem. So here is a common sense approach the NFL should adapt to avoid these public relations black eyes – because the league gets a lot of coverage over national anthem performances that go awry. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! The league, which supposedly has a right of refusal over these pregame and even halftime acts, can easily force the artists to sign binding contracts that demand they perform the songs as written. Sure, interpret all you want, the league can tell the artists. That's what makes you an artist. But don't alter lyrics to suit a personal agenda or feeling. Because that makes you an activist. articles.title: Rams dominate Raiders to get back on track as they seek to turn season around
articles.summary: The Rams are back in the win column, but have little room for error moving forward to contend for the NFC playoffs.
articles.body:
Through one half on Sunday, the Los Angeles Rams looked very much like the team many picked to win the Super Bowl. They raced out to 28-6 halftime lead over the Las Vegas Raiders that was big enough to overcome a pair of second-half turnovers. The Raiders never seriously threatened, and the Rams remained comfortably in control of a 35-21 win throughout the game.

The win snapped a two-game losing streak for the Rams, who entered Sunday 2-4 after being anointed in the preseason as the favorite to win the Super Bowl. A difficult road ahead remains for the Rams just to make the playoffs.

The Rams are now 3-4 with Sunday's win over a Raiders team with the same record after losing four straight. LA delivered the dominant win despite playing without key players on both sides of the ball.

All-Pro pass rusher Myles Garrett remains out with a knee injury that's sidelined him since Week 1. The Rams also played Sunday without All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie (groin), former All-Pro receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) and leading tackler Nathan Landman (concussion).

They looked little worse for wear due to the injuries with a strong effort on both sides of the ball. Matthew Stafford entered halftime having completed 17 of 19 passes for 148 yards with 3 touchdowns and no turnovers, channeling his MVP form from 2025.

His third touchdown pass to Puka Nacua extended the Rams lead to 21-3 late in the first half and made franchise history.

The touchdown pass was the 155th of his Rams career, moving him past Roman Gabriel for the most in franchise history.

The Rams added a fourth touchdown before the break on a 17-yard Kyren Williams run and entered halftime with a commanding 22-point lead.

A Stafford interception helped the Raiders cut their deficit to 28-18 in the fourth quarter. But a Blake Corum touchdown run extended the Rams' lead to 35-18 and iced the game with 6:34 remaining.

Stafford finished his day completing 23 of 29 passes for 195 yards with 3 touchdowns and 1 interception. The pick was hardly his fault as an on-target ball bounced off of tight end Colby Parkinson's hands and into those of linebacker Nakobe Dean. It raised Stafford's interception tally to seven after he threw eight in three of his previous four seasons.

Corum (93 yards 1 TD) and Williams (99 yards, 1 TD), meanwhile, led a rushing attack that tallied 199 yards on 5.2 yards per attempt as Los Angeles totaled 386 yards of total offense.

The Rams kept the Raiders out of the end zone until the fourth quarter. LA also failed to create a turnover and allowed Las Vegas to tally 350 yards in what added up to mixed performance. But it was largely encouraging on the heels of its 2-4 start, especially in the context of missing Garrett, McDuffie and Landman.

Rams have a long way to go to dig out of hole

Can the Rams keep this up? They have a favorable upcoming schedule with games against the Chargers, Commanders and Cardinals that they should expect to win if they consider themselves playoff contenders.

Even then, they'd be 6-4 with a difficult end-of season slate coming out of a Week 11 bye. The Rams finish the season with games against the Packers, Chiefs, 49ers, Cowboys, Seahawks, Bucs and Seahawks again.

In a stacked race for the NFC playoffs, there's little margin for error for the Rams.

articles.title: Lions Beat Packers, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Josh Jacobs, Gibbs, Jordan Love, Goff, More
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions picked up their first divisional win on Sunday, defeating the Green Bay Packers 20-17.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions picked up their first divisional win on Sunday, defeating the Green Bay Packers 20-17.

The Lions won the game on a walk-off field goal after capitalizing on a crucial error from the Packers.

The Packers got off to a bit of a rough start, missing a makeable field goal on their opening drive. The Lions then struck first, taking the ball 80 yards down the field and scoring on a pass from Jared Goff to Jameson Williams.

Green Bay answered right back, though, scoring on its next drive when Jordan Love found Tucker Kraft on a 14-yard touchdown pass.

The Lions added a field goal in the second quarter and got into field goal range again just before halftime, but Jahmyr Gibbs fumbled, squandering Detroit's chance to add more before the break.

On the first drive out of halftime, the Lions once again fumbled, and this one gave the Packers excellent field position. They took advantage of it, scoring on a pass from Love to Josh Jacobs.

Green Bay's lead didn't last long, though, as the Lions responded with a touchdown of their own to make it a 17-14 game.

Love threw an interception to start the fourth quarter, but it wasn't too costly, as the Lions failed to capitalize on it.

Love bounced back well from the interception and led the Packers to a field goal on the following drive to tie things up. From there, the Lions got bold and went for it on fourth down in their own territory but turned it over on downs.

The decision didn't come back to haunt them, though, as the Lions managed to block the Packers' go-ahead field goal attempt.

With the momentum of the blocked field goal on their side, the Lions marched down the field and drilled their own go-ahead field goal, leaving no time on the clock.

The win helps the Lions improve to 4-2 on the year, and they'll look to pick up another divisional win next week against the undefeated Minnesota Vikings.

articles.title: Rams Beat Raiders, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Stafford, Cousins, Puka, Jeanty, Top Players

The Los Angeles Rams defeated Kirk Cousins and the Las Vegas Raiders 35-21, led by a three-touchdown performance from Matthew Stafford.

The Rams entered Sunday's road matchup against the Raiders as 3.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , exceeding expectations after holding Las Vegas to six first-half points.

Despite a 15-0 run, the Raiders came up short, suffering their fourth straight loss to fall to 3-4 on the season. Las Vegas has not won since Week 3, when it defeated the New Orleans Saints.

Meanwhile, the Rams snapped a two-game losing streak with the victory, improving to 3-4 on the season.

The Rams scored on four of their five first-half possessions to take a commanding 28-6 lead into halftime.

Stafford connected with tight end Davis Allen for touchdowns in both the first and second quarters before finding Puka Nacua for an 11-yard score. Kyren Williams added a 17-yard rushing touchdown to cap Los Angeles' dominant half.

Las Vegas managed just two field goals, missing another in the first quarter as the Rams' defense forced two punts and a turnover on downs to keep the Raiders out of the end zone.

The third quarter was a struggle for both teams, as the Raiders turned the ball over on downs twice while the Rams were forced to punt twice and lost a fumble by Williams.

The Raiders mounted a furious fourth-quarter comeback, with Cousins connecting with Tre Tucker for a touchdown before Ashton Jeanty added a 15-yard touchdown reception to cap a 15-0 scoring run. Las Vegas' defense also came up big with an interception on Stafford.

Los Angeles found its first score of the second half on a Blake Corum touchdown run to regain control, extending its lead to 17 points with just over 6:30 remaining in the game.

Despite a field goal by the Raiders on the following possession, the Rams were able to kneel it out to secure the road victory.

The Rams will host their in-state rivals, the Los Angeles Chargers, next Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET, while the Raiders head cross-country to face the New York Jets at 1 p.m. ET the same day.

articles.title: Raiders HC Talks Possibility of Starting Fernando Mendoza, Benching Kirk Cousins After Rams Loss
articles.summary: After a 3-0 start to the season, the Las Vegas Raiders have dropped their last four and are ready to consider any necessary changes.
articles.body:
After a 3-0 start to the season, the Las Vegas Raiders have dropped their last four and are ready to consider any necessary changes.

Even benching Kirk Cousins for rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza.

"I think at this point, we're thinking about everything," head coach Klint Kubiak said after Sunday's loss to the Los Angeles Rams. "How to fix our problems, how to fix our issues in the red zone, in the third quarter. Personnel, scheme, we've got to talk about all of it."

Despite the Raiders' struggles, Cousins has been mostly solid under center, throwing for 1,877 yards, 16 touchdowns and five interceptions. His passing touchdown total leads the NFL.

Cousins threw for 295 yards and a pair of scores in Sunday's loss to the Rams. The Raiders would have liked to see him be a bit more effecient and capitalize on red zone opportunities more, but he at least didn't have any egregious errors.

Las Vegas' main issue has been on defense, as it has given up 30, 45, 33 and 35 points in its last four games, respectively. That will surely be something to address in the coming weeks as the Raiders try to turn things around.

Still, it could be worth giving Mendoza a shot, especially since the Raiders are still in a rebuilding phase.

Mendoza, the top pick in the 2026 NFL draft out of Indiana, came in for Cousins at the end of the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the New England Patriots and threw for 48 yards on 6-of-8 passes.

Las Vegas drafted Mendoza, hoping he'd be the franchise quarterback for years to come, but the original plan was to let Cousins take the reins this year before potentially giving Mendoza a shot next year.

Whether Kubiak has decided to change the course of action and go with Mendoza this year remains to be seen.

The Raiders will face the New York Jets, one of the league's top passing defenses, next week, so it would be a tough first test for the young player.

articles.title: 49ers Called Out for Losing ‘$40 Million Per Year’ Edge Rusher
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers called out for losing "$40 million per year" edge rusher. The post 49ers Called Out for Losing ‘$40 Million Per Year’ Edge Rusher appeare...
articles.body:
In 2026, we're finally seeing the player the Washington Commanders thought they drafted with the No. 2 overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft

While Chase Young is doing it two teams later with the New Orleans Saints, he's doing it at such a high level that he's now second in the NFL with 7.0 sacks through 7 games, following a dominant performance in his team's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris.

Young trails Houston Texans edge rusher and NFL All-Pro Will Anderson Jr. by just a half-sack.

For a team that struggles to get to the passer, it's likely a bitter pill to swallow for the Commanders and their fans, who cut bait on Young with a trade to the San Francisco 49ers midway through the 2023 season.

It's also a bitter pill for the 49ers and their fans to swallow as they could have had Young for a relatively paltry sum before the 2024 season.

"Chase Young has 22.5 sacks since leaving the 49ers after the 2023 season," The Associated Press wrote on X . "No one on Niners has more than 11 in that span."

"Chase Young is having a terrific season in New Orleans," The Athletic's David Aldridge wrote on his official X account on Sunday. "Didn't work out in D.C., obviously, but he's resurrected his career with the Saints. Good for him."

"Saints don't play many island games, so if you're just watching them for the first time … this is how Chase Young has been playing for the last two seasons," Saints reporter Nick Underhill wrote on X . "He's about to be a $40+ million/year man."

Chase Young Headed for Massive New Contract

Headed into his 8th season and now with the New Orleans Saints — his 3rd team — Bleacher Report's Gary Davenport called Young's next big-money deal 1 of the NFL's "Most Important Contract Decisions" in 2026.

Young signed a 3-year, $51 million contract with the Saints in March 2025.

"Last year, it finally came together for Saints edge-rusher Chase Young," Davenport wrote on August 2. "It didn't look like it was going to — the former No. 2 overall pick missed the season's first five games with a calf injury. But once Young was back on the field, he caught fire—a career-high 10 sacks in 12 games … Young is under contract through 2027 at a bargain price relative to what other high-end edge-rushers make. If he can back up last year's numbers with a hot start in 2026, extending the 27-year-old now could save the Saints a boatload of scratch down the road."

Chase Young Part of Dreadful Run of Draft Picks

After securing the first big-time payday of his career, Young delivered his best season in 2025 as the Saints were 1 of the NFL's most-improved teams down the stretch under rookie head coach Kellen Moore .

Young's deal was being singled out as one of the NFL's "Best Free Agent Signings" of the 2025 cycle by PFF's Bradley Locker .

It's a far cry from when Young's time with the Commanders ended midway through the 2023 season as one of the biggest busts in franchise history.

"The Saints made a rarely large move when they retained Young on a three-year, $51 million contract to prevent him from leaving," Locker wrote. "In turn, Young absolutely dominated when on the field with an 86.3 PFF pass-rush grade and a 15.2% pass-rush win rate. The former No. 2 overall pick appears to have settled into form with the Saints."

Young was part of an incredible run of 1st-round picks who didn't pan out for the Commanders — 6 picks in 5 years from 2019 to 2023 no longer on their roster by the end of the 2024 season.

The biggest bust of the bunch was Young. Following a torn ACL suffered in Week 10 of the 2021 regular season, Young missed 22 of the next 25 regular-season games, including all but 3 games in 2022 — a 2-season stretch in which he had just 1.5 sacks.

Young revamped his career in 2023 with 7.5 sacks while playing for both the Commanders and the San Francisco 49ers after a midseason trade and was a role player as the 49ers made it to the Super Bowl.

Young took the momentum from his time with the 49ers and parlayed that into a 1-year, $13 million contract with the Saints in 2024, when he played in every regular-season game for the first time in his career and finished with 5.5 sacks, 8 TFL and 21 QB hits.

articles.title: Former Texas A&M star Cashius Howell records first NFL sack
articles.summary: Former Texas A&M defensive end Cashius Howell recorded his first NFL sack, reaching an important milestone in his rookie season.
articles.body:
Former Texas A&M defensive end Cashius Howell reached an important milestone Sunday, recording his first NFL sack for the Cincinnati Bengals .

The second-round pick had been generating pressure in his first several appearances but hadn't yet brought down a quarterback for an official sack. Texas A&M Football celebrated the accomplishment on social media, sharing a video of the play.

Howell's first sack comes after a promising start to his professional career. Through his first two games, he recorded seven quarterback pressures, ranking second among NFL rookies at the time, according to Pro Football Focus.

Howell also posted a 17% pass-rush win rate during that stretch, showing his ability to consistently challenge opposing offensive linemen despite limited opportunities.

The production should come as no surprise to Texas A&M fans. Howell finished his final collegiate season with 11.5 sacks, earning SEC Defensive Player of the Year honors before Cincinnati selected him with the 41st overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft. His transition to the NFL has included competing for snaps in Cincinnati's defensive rotation, but his ability to pressure quarterbacks has remained one of his strengths.

Sunday's milestone represents another step forward for Howell as he looks to establish himself as a consistent contributor to the Bengals' defense.

articles.title: Peyton Manning’s Role in Colts GM Search Clarified After Chris Ballard Firing
articles.summary: Peyton Manning is one of the greatest players, if not the greatest, to ever play for the Indianapolis Colts. The former quarterback is one of the most decora...
articles.body:
Peyton Manning is one of the greatest players, if not the greatest, to ever play for the Indianapolis Colts . The former quarterback is one of the most decorated players in American football history. He has won the Super Bowl two times, and is a five-time NFL Most Valuable Player.

The Colts have not found the same success since Manning's departure. He has now taken an important decision regarding his former team.

Peyton Manning not expected to take Colts GM role

The Colts recently fired general manager Chris Ballard after more than nine seasons. While in charge at the franchise, the team had a 72-82-1 record, made two playoff appearances, and started 14 different quarterbacks after Andrew Luck's retirement. Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon has said the franchise will conduct a thorough search for the next general manager. One of the names initially linked to the search was none other than Manning.

However, according to league sources cited by ESPN's Adam Schefter , the legendary quarterback is not expected to emerge as a candidate for the Colts' vacant general manager position. The franchise have not contacted Manning about the role, and the Hall of Fame quarterback is not anticipated to pursue it.

Manning has not prepared for or expressed interest in becoming an NFL general manager. His post-playing career includes running Omaha Productions, co-hosting the ManningCast on ESPN's Monday Night Football package, and handling commercial commitments. He also has two children in high school, further limiting time for a position that demands full-time, day-to-day operational focus. Sources indicated the timing is unsuitable given these existing responsibilities.

The same sources also said that Manning remains open to considering NFL opportunities in the future, but only for those that involve higher-profile executive or ownership-adjacent roles similar to those held by other former players. Some examples include Tom Brady's role as minority owner and adviser with the Las Vegas Raiders, Matt Ryan as president of football for the Atlanta Falcons, and Tony Boselli as executive vice president of football operations for the Jacksonville Jaguars. Manning has previously talked about leading an NFL team from the front office.

Peyton Manning once spoke about running football team

Manning previously shared his thoughts on running a football team in the future. In an interview with the Denver Post , he said, "I don't think that's anywhere on my radar by any means. I love being an ambassador for the Broncos and for the Colts, for the University of Tennessee. Obviously, living here I get to go to all the Broncos games. I was out at the facility the other day. Our kids do sports in the area around Dove Valley, so I'm probably at the facility a couple times a week."

He added, "I'm excited about still being a part of the team and being part of the community. . . . I still feel an attachment and have really enjoyed getting to know the Walton-Penner family as well. But as far as running a team, I don't think that's on my radar."

While Peyton Manning will not be interested in the role, the Colts will have to select a suitable GM for their future.

articles.title: Dolphins Accused of Letting Five-Time Pro Bowler’s Career ‘Die’ Through 2018 Browns Trade
articles.summary: Former Five-time Pro Bowler Jarvis Landry spent four seasons with the Miami Dolphins after they selected him No. 63 overall in the 2014 NFL Draft. Miami plac...
articles.body:
Former Five-time Pro Bowler Jarvis Landry spent four seasons with the Miami Dolphins after they selected him No. 63 overall in the 2014 NFL Draft. Miami placed the franchise tag on the wide receiver in 2018, then traded him to the Cleveland Browns in March of that year for a 2018 fourth-round pick and a 2019 seventh-round pick.

Before the trade, Landry made three straight Pro Bowls in South Florida and set an NFL record with 400 receptions through his first four seasons. However, he never wanted to leave. Recently, he called out the Dolphins and former head coach Adam Gase for sending him to Cleveland.

Jarvis Landry accuses Adam Gase of trying to end his NFL career

Landry's career did not stall after Gase sent him to the Browns. He caught 81 passes for 976 yards and four touchdowns in his first season in Cleveland and earned a fourth straight Pro Bowl nod.

In 2019, he posted a career-high 1,174 receiving yards on 83 receptions and made his fifth consecutive Pro Bowl. But the problem was Cleveland's record, because they had gone a combined 1-31 in 2016 and 2017.

"I did not want to leave from Miami," Landry said on his 4th and South podcast. "That was a situation with a coach that he just decided that he was going to try to send me to Cleveland and let my career die and be over with. But when we really take a look at it, bro, we was talking numbers of s*** that I had earned."

Initially, Landry's individual success did little to change Cleveland's losing culture. Under head coach Hue Jackson and interim coach Gregg Williams, the Browns finished the 2018 season with a 7-8-1 record.

The coaching carousel spun the following year again, but under first-time head coach Freddie Kitchens, the Browns regressed to a disappointing 6-10 finish in 2019. Despite the team's struggles, Landry remained a bright spot, earning Pro Bowl nods in both seasons.

The breakthrough finally came in 2020 under a completely new regime. With the hiring of general manager Andrew Berry and first-year head coach Kevin Stefanski, Cleveland's identity shifted. The Browns surged to an 11-5 record, capturing their first winning season since 2007 and ending a league-high 17-year playoff drought.

Landry drove the offense in that season. He missed one game due to COVID-19 protocols but still led the team's receivers with 72 receptions for 840 yards and three touchdowns in 15 games.

Landry criticized Gase after the 2018 trade, stating openly that he believed Gase sent him to Cleveland "to die." When Gase later coached the New York Jets, he addressed the statement. He admitted he threatened to trade players to Cleveland during a team meeting but claimed it was a joke. "I don't remember exactly what I said," Gase said. "It was supposed to be a joke."

However, Cleveland released Landry after four seasons, and he finished his career with the New Orleans Saints in 2022.

articles.title: Giants’ Cam Skattebo calls out NFL double standard after ridiculous penalty during Texans game
articles.summary: The New York Giants are 4-2-1 on the season after defeating the Houston Texans 27-21 on Sunday. It was a great performance for running back Cam Skattebo, as...
articles.body:
The New York Giants are 4-2-1 on the season after defeating the Houston Texans 27-21 on Sunday. It was a great performance for running back Cam Skattebo , as he played a key part in helping his team get the win. However, after the game, Skattebo had some choice words for the NFL after being penalized for lowering his helmet.

The 24-year-old was given a 15-yard unnecessary roughness penalty during the contest after delivering a hard hit on Texans safety M.J. Stewart. After the game, Skattebo claimed that he has no intention of changing his playing style and called out the NFL a bit for consistently hyping him up for how he plays football, but then turning around and penalizing him for playing hard.

"The NFL loves to post me when I do stuff like that," Skattebo said. "But then also wants to take stuff from me. If I'm going to continue to get flagged for it, or fined for it, I guess I'm going to play for free."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

While the second-year pro did lower his shoulder and deliver a hard hit, the contact looked rather similar to what you'd see in old Mike Alstott highlights. Skattebo just ran through Stewart on the play, and it would have been a clean play back in the day.

Truth be told, the NFL has seemingly enjoyed sharing Cam Skattebo hits . Whether it's commercials or highlights, the former Arizona State Sun Devils star has built a reputation for being a hard-hitting running back.

After essentially being benched in the previous game, Skattebo turned things around against the Texans. He finished the day with 124 rushing yards and a touchdown on 17 attempts.

articles.title: Falcons hand 49ers first defeat of NFL season, Vikings remain unbeaten
articles.summary: Michael Penix threw for three touchdowns and the Atlanta defense forced four turnovers as the Falcons beat San Francisco 29-20 to deal the 49ers their first...
articles.body:
Michael Penix threw for three touchdowns and the Atlanta defense forced four turnovers as the Falcons beat San Francisco 29-20 to deal the 49ers their first defeat of the NFL season on Sunday.

San Francisco quarterback Brock Purdy was intercepted twice, George Kittle and Kaelon Black gave up fumbles and a thigh injury to Christian McCaffrey further hindered the 49ers' depleted receiving corps.

One week after he was stretchered off after taking a knee to the head, Atlanta's rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels intercepted a Purdy pass intended for Jordan Watkins with 2:34 remaining and recovered Kittle's fumble with less than a minute to go to secure their first home win of the season and improve to 3-4.

"It was all complementary football," Penix said. "Offense, defense, special teams, everybody played well today."

Penix connected with tight end Nick Muse for a touchdown to keep the Falcons within striking distance in the first half and hit Kyle Pitts for a TD that put Atlanta ahead in the third quarter.

He found Drake London with a 21-yard touchdown pass in the fourth.

McCaffrey had capped a 10-play, 64-yard opening drive with a one-yard touchdown leap on fourth down to give San Francisco a quick 7-0 lead.

But he missed much of the first half with a thigh injury and despite his return in the second half the 49ers couldn't come back.

"Any time you have four turnovers like that and you get zero, it's real tough to win," 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said. "Too sloppy to win."

While the 49ers fell to 6-1, the Minnesota Vikings remained unbeaten, holding the Indianapolis Colts scoreless in the second half in a 16-10 victory that saw them improve to 6-0.

Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray threw a five-yard touchdown pass to T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter and Will Reichard kicked a 52-yard field goal with 1:39 remaining.

Minnesota's Harrison Smith picked off Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in the final minute to preserve the win. It was the 40th career interception for the 15-year veteran.

The Vikings remained as one of two unbeaten teams. The Kansas City Chiefs were seeking to improve to 6-0 when they took on the Super Bowl champion Seahawks in Seattle.

Sunday's action kicked off in Paris, where Pittsburgh quarterback Aaron Rodgers threw for 212 yards and a milestone touchdown to lead the Steelers to a 16-10 victory over the New Orleans Saints in the league's first regular-season game in the French capital.

Rodgers hit Darnell Washington with a four-yard TD pass to give the Steelers a 10-3 lead late in the second quarter, his 540th regular-season touchdown pass moving him into solo third place on the all-time list ahead of Peyton Manning (539).

The Los Angeles Rams snapped a two-game skid in emphatic style, beating the Raiders 35-21 in Las Vegas.

Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford threw for 195 yards and three touchdowns, all in the first half. He became the franchise leader in scoring passes -- an honor Stafford also holds with the Detroit Lions.

"More importantly, happy for our guys," Stafford said. "We've had some tough losses late in games this year, played good enough football to win games and hadn't gotten it done ... proud of our resolve and our ability to get the win."

In Houston, Devin Singletary ran 30 yards for a touchdown in overtime to lift the New York Giants to a 27-21 upset win over the Texans.

In Detroit, Jake Bates kicked a 22-yard field goal as time expired to give the Lions a 20-17 victory over the Green Bay Packers.

Cincinnati quarterback Joe Burrow threw four touchdown passes in the second half as the Bengals rallied to beat the Ravens 35-13 in Baltimore.

Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson piloted his fifth fourth-quarter game-winning drive of the season, capped by Andre Szmyt's 32-yard field goal as time expired in the Browns' 27-24 victory over the Tennessee Titans in Nashville.

And the Miami Dolphins earned their first win of the season, beating the New York Jets 28-25 in New Jersey.
